question: The price of 3 notebooks and 6 pen is Rs. 3000. With the same money one can buy a notebooks and 12 pen. Raju wants to buy 15 pen, how much will he have to pay ?
solution:
**Given:**

Price of 3 notebooks and 6 pens = ₹3000

Price of 1 notebook and 12 pens = ₹3000

**Calculation:**

Price of one notebook = x

Price of one pen = y

From the first condition:

3x + 6y = 3000 ...(1)

From the second condition:

x + 12y = 3000 ...(2)

Multiply equation (1) by 1 and equation (2) by 3:

3x + 6y = 3000 ...(1)

3x + 36y = 9000 ...(3)

Subtract equation (1) from (3):

30y = 6000

y = 200 (price of one pen)

For 15 pens:

Cost = 15 × 200

Cost = 3000

Therefore, Raju will have to pay Rs. 3000 for 15 pens.

The answer is option 1) Rs. 3000

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

Let the price of 1 notebook be ( N ) and 1 pen be ( P ).

3N + 6P = 3000

N + 12P = 3000

From the second equation, ( N = 3000 - 12P )

Substitute ( N ) in the first equation:

3(3000 - 12P) + 6P = 3000

⇒ 9000 - 36P + 6P = 3000

⇒ 9000 - 30P = 3000

⇒ 30P = 6000

⇒ P = 200

Substitute ( P ) in ( N = 3000 - 12P ):

N = 3000 - 12 × 200

⇒ N = 3000 - 2400

⇒ N = 600

Cost for 15 pens = 15 × P

⇒ Cost = 15 × 200

⇒ Cost = ₹3000

**∴ Raju will have to pay ₹3000 for 15 pens.**
